passage: At Kalyani's housewarming, Sarika made a joke about how Kalyani had "finally learnt to cook something other than instant noodles" in front of the neighbours. People smiled. Kalyani's smile flickered, and she went to refill the water jug. Sarika felt it land wrong. Later, in the kitchen, Sarika said, "Kalyani, I'm sorry. That joke wasn't okay, especially in front of everyone." Kalyani wiped her hands. "It did sting a bit." "I know. I shouldn't have said it. It wasn't funny." Sarika did not add anything else. Kalyani nodded and gave a small, tired smile. "Thank you for saying that."

qa.q: What did Sarika joke about at the housewarming?
qa.a: That Kalyani had finally learnt to cook something other than instant noodles.

qa.q: What was Sarika feeling after seeing Kalyani's smile flicker?
qa.a: Regret and discomfort, since Sarika felt the joke had landed wrong and went to apologise.

qa.q: What made Sarika's apology work?
qa.a: Sarika said sorry, said the joke wasn't okay, and added nothing about intent or Kalyani being sensitive.

qa.q: How might Kalyani feel after hearing "I'm sorry"?
qa.a: Acknowledged and a bit relieved, though still tired. Kalyani admitted it stung and thanked Sarika for saying it.

grounding: Someone realises a joke hurt and says sorry cleanly, without adding but you are too sensitive.

passage:
"Vasudha, got a minute?" said Harish, standing at her desk after the meeting.
"Sure."
"Earlier, when I did that impression of your accent, it wasn't okay. I saw your face. I'm sorry."
"It was uncomfortable," said Vasudha. "Everyone looked."
"I know. I shouldn't have done it. I won't do it again."
"I'd have liked you to say it in the meeting, honestly."
"That's fair. Should I say something to the team?"
"Maybe a line. Not a speech."
"Okay. Thank you for telling me."
Vasudha nodded. "Thank you for not saying it was only a joke."

qa.q: What did Harish apologise for?
qa.a: Doing an impression of Vasudha's accent in the meeting.

qa.q: How did Vasudha feel about the impression in the meeting?
qa.a: Uncomfortable and exposed, since everyone looked at Vasudha after it.

qa.q: What did Harish do that repaired trust?
qa.a: Harish apologised plainly, said the impression was not okay, took the feedback, and offered to say a line to the team.

qa.q: How might Harish have felt when Vasudha said everyone looked?
qa.a: Probably regretful and ready to own it, since Harish answered 'I know. I shouldn't have done it' and offered to say something to the team.

grounding: Someone realises a joke hurt and says I am sorry, that was not okay, without a defence of intent.

passage:
At dinner last month, my friends were laughing about driving tests. I said, "At least none of us failed three times like Kalyani!" Everyone laughed. Kalyani laughed too, then went quiet and started picking at her rice.
I noticed, but I told myself it was fine. We always joke.
On the drive home, I kept seeing her face. The next morning I called her. I wanted to say, "I was only joking, you know I didn't mean it." I stopped myself. That would be about me.
I said, "Kalyani, I'm sorry. That joke was not okay. I embarrassed you in front of everyone." There was a pause. Then she said, "Thank you. It really stung. I've been so stressed about the fourth attempt." We talked for half an hour.
I'm Lavanya, and I'm learning that "sorry" without "but" works better.

qa.q: How many times had Kalyani failed her driving test?
qa.a: Three times.

qa.q: How did Lavanya feel on the drive home?
qa.a: Lavanya felt uneasy and guilty, remembering Kalyani's face.

qa.q: What made Lavanya's apology clean?
qa.a: It named the joke as not okay and admitted embarrassing Kalyani, without adding 'I was only joking' or blaming her sensitivity.

qa.q: How did Kalyani feel after the apology?
qa.a: She felt relieved and grateful, and opened up about her stress over the fourth attempt.

grounding: Shows a young adult realising a joke hurt and apologising cleanly without defending her intent, which repairs trust.

passage:
Team lead's note, customer support, Thursday.
At Monday's stand-up, Sharmila joked that Parveen "types like my grandmother," after Parveen took a while to share her screen. A few people laughed. Parveen's face flushed and she kept her camera off for the rest of the meeting.
Sharmila came to me on Tuesday, looking uncomfortable, and asked if she should say something. I asked what she wanted to say. She said, "Sorry, but it was just a joke." I suggested dropping the "but."
On Wednesday I heard her in the pantry: "Parveen, I'm sorry about Monday. That joke wasn't okay, and I embarrassed you." Parveen said, "Thanks for saying it." Today they were sharing lunch. I'll check in with Parveen next week to see how she's feeling.

qa.q: What did Sharmila say Parveen types like?
qa.a: Like her grandmother.

qa.q: What was Sharmila feeling when she came to the team lead on Tuesday?
qa.a: Sharmila felt uncomfortable and uneasy about the joke, but still wanted to defend it as 'just a joke'.

qa.q: What did the team lead suggest, and why did it help?
qa.a: Dropping the 'but', so Sharmila's apology didn't defend her intent and could repair trust faster.

qa.q: How did Parveen respond to the clean apology?
qa.a: She thanked Sharmila, and by Thursday they were sharing lunch.

grounding: Shows someone realising a joke hurt and apologising cleanly, without defending intent, which repairs trust.

passage:
Friday night
Today at the office lunch, Tenzin brought momos, and I said, "Of course! Do you people eat anything else?" Some people laughed. Tenzin smiled but went very quiet and ate his lunch fast.
All afternoon it bothered me. I told myself, he knows I didn't mean it. But I also knew what I'd done: I made his whole culture a punchline.
Before leaving, I went to his desk. I wanted to say, "Sorry, but you know I was joking." I didn't. I said, "Tenzin, I'm sorry. That was a lazy, stupid joke, and it wasn't okay." He looked up, surprised. Then he said, "Thanks. I hear that one a lot, actually." That made me feel worse, and also glad I said it.
He offered me a momo. I said yes.
Shalini

qa.q: What did Tenzin bring for lunch?
qa.a: Momos.

qa.q: How did Shalini feel all afternoon after the joke?
qa.a: Shalini felt uneasy and guilty, knowing the joke made Tenzin's culture a punchline.

qa.q: What made Shalini's apology a clean one?
qa.a: It named the joke as lazy and not okay, without adding 'but you know I was joking'.

qa.q: How did Tenzin respond to the apology?
qa.a: He was surprised, thanked Shalini, said he hears that joke a lot, and offered a momo.

grounding: Shows a young adult realising a joke hurt and apologising cleanly without defending intent, which begins to repair trust.
